newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says EU scraps import tax on cotton yarn.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says EU scraps import tax on cotton yarn.

text.p: The European Union (EU) scrapped with immediate effect a tax on cotton yarn imports from Turkey, Turkey's state-run Anatolian news agency said.

It said the tax, imposed at 4.6 to 12.1 percent on various cotton yarns since March 1992 by the EU, was scrapped because there had not been any complaints since its imposition by any member countries about Turkey's cotton yarn sales to the EU.
It said the decree on the abolition was announced by the EU on Friday.
Some Turkish yarn industrialists said the abolition of the tax would nevertheless not boost Turkey's yarn exports back to where they were before the tax was imposed in 1992.

"The European yarn sector has grown since the tax was imposed and also Turkish yarn producers have opted for other areas like weaving and knitting," said Ertekin Ashapoglu, a board member of Istanbul Textile Exporters Association.
"Therefore I do not think our exports will reach levels of 100,000 tonnes a year because of the abolition. Maybe a rise of 25 to 30 percent is possible," he said.
Turkey's cotton yarn exports to the EU was about 25,000 tonnes in 1996, he said.
Some companies think exports may now rise to 75,000 tonnes.
